card_verdicts.reason: Explicit n-descent literature canonicalizes genus-one/cover models but does not replace the exact repo forward/inverse maps, denominator opens, exceptional loci, or integrality firewall.

Elliptic-logarithm and quadratic-Chabauty algorithms can supply a complete auxiliary point set after extra model/MW/height hypotheses; the exact integral iff-transfer contract itself remains unchanged.
The pullback/accounting discipline is already complete; literature methods are upstream solvers that may supply the certified complete auxiliary point set.
Keep strict full-group semantics, but expose separately controlled finite-index/index/saturation data for downstream sieve/Chabauty methods that do not require a full group proof.
Finite squareclass branches can feed covering collections/descent only after each branch is identified with an exact cover/torsor/Selmer object.
Bruin-Stoll generalizes good-prime CRT to arbitrary exact finite MW quotients/local admissible subsets, arbitrary rank, controlled finite-index subgroups, and richer local information.
Its receiver-restricted interface is already method-agnostic and can route to Chabauty, elliptic Chabauty, quadratic Chabauty, MW sieve, or covering descent once exact hypotheses are materialized.
Parameter-dependent reservoirs do not give the fixed finite support required for the reviewed descent/covering/S-integral terminal methods.
Exact involution quotient is a strong preterminal adapter, but literature Chabauty methods require a further exact curve/field/extension/rationality dictionary.
Kummer-style simultaneous squares are promising 2-cover data, but the frozen card does not establish an actual covering/Selmer/torsor class.
General birational literature does not improve the exact iff common-factor compression; its output should feed a separate terminal method.
Its main literature family is finite-field point counting/Hasse-Weil, outside this elliptic/MW rational-point Phase 2.
